slot.brief: Arrange letters of a word so that certain vowels are always together and a particular pair never together; combine cases carefully

stem: How many distinct arrangements of the letters of BALLOON have all vowels together, while B and N are not adjacent?

verdicts.working: Treat AOO as one block, with 3 internal arrangements. The five objects are this block, B, N, L, L: 5!/2 × 3 = 180. With B and N adjacent, combine them as BN or NB: 2 × (4!/2) × 3 = 72. Thus 180 − 72 = 108.

working:
Vowels together: internal arrangements $=\dfrac{3!}{2!}=3$
Outer arrangements $=\dfrac{5!}{2!}=60$
With B and N adjacent: $2\cdot\dfrac{4!}{2!}=24$
Required $=3(60-24)=108$

Independent check: Treat AOO as one block, with 3 internal arrangements. The five objects are this block, B, N, L, L: 5!/2 × 3 = 180. With B and N adjacent, combine them as BN or NB: 2 × (4!/2) × 3 = 72. Thus 180 − 72 = 108.
solution:
The vowels AOO stay together in $\dfrac{3!}{2!}=3$ internal arrangements. Treat them as one block; the five objects have $\dfrac{5!}{2!}=60$ arrangements.
If B and N are adjacent, combine them as one object: $2\times\dfrac{4!}{2!}=24$ arrangements of the outer objects.
$$3(60-24)=108$$
